strengths: The motivation is relevant to visual recognition: avoiding spurious correlations does not ensure robustness when an invariant cue becomes occluded or unavailable. Encouraging complementary predictive cues is a worthwhile objective.

H-CMNIST provides a useful controlled diagnostic of feature removal. In Table 1, ASGDRO improves shape-only accuracy from GDRO's 61.44% to 69.17%, supporting an increased ability to exploit the harder invariant feature.

The empirical evaluation is broad and reports useful gains. CelebA worst-group accuracy improves from GDRO's 87.2% to 91.0%; DomainBed average accuracy reaches 65.9%; and adding ASGDRO to DPLCLIP improves its average from 72.6% to 74.0%. These results support practical usefulness.

The combination of adaptive sharpness minimization and group reweighting is straightforward to reuse. Pseudocode, a code link, and appendix details covering architectures, hyperparameter searches, model selection, and repeated runs support reproducibility.
weaknesses: Theorem 1 is false as stated, undermining the central theoretical contribution. Under Appendix A.4's construction, take Y=1 and any simplex vector lambda. Then R(theta)=0.5(1-sum_i theta_i)^2, and the stated Euclidean perturbation objective satisfies max_{||epsilon||_2<=rho} R(lambda+epsilon)=p*rho^2/2, independently of lambda. Single-feature and uniform solutions therefore tie. The proof introduces a lambda-dependent gradient factor without justification; its first-order gradient term also vanishes at these interpolating solutions. An adaptive perturbation constraint would require a different statement and derivation.

The reduction from SIL to parameter-space flatness contains additional unsupported steps. Joint conditional invariance does not imply invariance or predictive sufficiency of every feature subset, as asserted in Section 3.2. Section 3.3 also equates the maximum risk over finitely many invariant mechanisms with the maximum over an enclosing parameter ball; containment establishes only an inequality. Low-risk interpolation paths do not establish low risk throughout that ball. These gaps affect the claimed connection between flatness and robustness to missing features.

The evaluated algorithm differs materially from the analyzed objective. Section 3.5 replaces environment-specific adversarial perturbations with one perturbation derived from average empirical risk in every experiment except the toy example. Environment gradients can cancel in this average even when their individual gradients are large. No approximation guarantee or comparison between the two implementations establishes that the practical update preserves the claimed protection across environments.

The experiments support improved accuracy more strongly than the proposed mechanism. H-CMNIST is the only controlled missing-invariant-feature evaluation and contains two invariant cues; ASGDRO's shape-only accuracy remains 69.17±6.19% across three seeds. Standard benchmark accuracy, selected Grad-CAM examples, and smaller Hessian eigenvalues do not establish that multiple independently useful cues cause the gains or ensure robustness when cues disappear. This limitation matters because achieving SIL is the paper's distinguishing claim beyond combining existing optimization components.

There are smaller reporting and reproducibility issues: RxRx1 accuracy is 32.2±0.2% in Table 3 but 30.5±0.1% in Figure 7, and Appendix A.9 supplies uncertainty for DPLCLIP variants without the corresponding base-ASGDRO results referenced by Table 4. These are correctable issues. My weak-reject recommendation is primarily determined by the invalid central theorem and the unsupported connection between SIL and the implemented algorithm, despite the worthwhile empirical gains.
